parts.name: The rule by which every operation is placed, with the two riders that make the columns decide anything
parts.statement: Each operation is placed by what it minimally needs to be instantiated: at one call if an execution with what its context carries suffices; across calls if continuity of a process or a carrier suffices; only with a record or a harness if it needs a history with precedence and receipts, a program around the agent, or a declared input from outside; never if the theory's definition needs something no arrangement at the grain of text supplies. Two riders. First, a declared index the call's own context carries (the contract, the grain of the document) does not move a row out of "at one call"; a declared index that is an attribution about the system making the claim (the boundary, the continuity) does, because a system cannot declare those of itself without the circularity the theory forbids. Second, a column says what instantiating needs, not what establishing needs; where establishing needs more, the note says so.

word_list.plain_word: what the theory records and does not supply

word_list.quote: A verdict that depends on one of these is a verdict given the input; where the input is missing, the verdict is unsettled and the semantics says so rather than choosing the input from the verdict wanted.

(R) depends on (F1)–(F2) and physical provenance. (K1) depends on (E). Deploy depends on (R) and (CT1). Build depends on histories and (E). (N), (G) depend on Deploy and Build. operations_table.operation: Organizations: ports, components, admitted edits (Part II) — (O)
operations_table.holder: HV file 52, close marking, item 1: "**Shape.** FULL (the question frozen, parts and jobs listed, a change list, tests run, a mark on every part, and the report's seven headings), PART, or NONE." With H62: "All twenty-four FULL in shape; no CANNOT". The theory's side: "A deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports. An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port; it does not add an equation beside an incompatible one. A changed rule is a changed component." (Part II — Organizations and their changes, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs on material handed to it. The ports are the document's passages and the components the dependences the reader names; the call needs the document and nothing else. What would move it: if the organization wanted is the agent's own at the grain of text, that is a declared input, not something a call instantiates, and the row moves to "only with a record or a harness" (builder A's M1); or if the admitted edits include changes only a rig can make.

operations_table.operation: The query, the baseline, the respect of a question (Part III) — (Q)
operations_table.holder: "What a question asks, production, identification, obstruction, rule-status or purpose-achievement, is fixed by the type of \(\mathcal Q\) and the shape of \(C\), not by a label." (Part III — Questions, The respect is the query, 10 and 11 (reworded)).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs. The record shows a call fixing a query and two calls under identical framing fixing different ones: H62, "The frozen question moved on F4. Two runs under file 31 (m1-r1, m2-r1) froze 'why does the room, or the reader, come to believe him'". What would move it: the identity of the query across calls is not instantiated at a call — it is carried by the frozen question handed in, which is across calls, and phase 3's question-identity field (P3.3) exists for exactly that.

operations_table.operation: The contract: its changes and its stated scope (Part III) — contract
operations_table.holder: "A contract is a declared subset of the physically admitted changes, and a stated scope is what makes it one." (Part III — Questions, Scope, and a question that can be wrong, 11 only).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs. Writing a change list and stating a scope needs the document and the question. Two things are not at one call and are not this row: checking that every excluded physically admitted edit is excluded by a stated scope needs the physically admitted set, which the physical module supplies; and a constructed contract needs a construction witness (row 11). What would move it: requiring the check rather than the statement moves the row to "only with a record or a harness".

operations_table.operation: Kinds as edit-signatures (Part II) — (K)
operations_table.holder: "These are descriptions of patterns in (K), not additional data. The semantics never asks whether a component \"is\" a cause. It asks what its signature is." (Part II — Organizations and their changes, Kinds are edit-signatures, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs. On a document the admitted edits are edits to the text, which a call can make; on the target the document describes they are imagined, so the reader's poke is a claim about what would happen rather than a change made. The record puts poke lowest of the eleven between markers (35 of 48, H64), which bears on the measurement and not on the operation. What would move it: any kind-claim whose separating edit has to be made in the world moves the row to "only with a record or a harness".

operations_table.operation: Checking an account: (F1), (F2), (A), non-circular, non-vacuous (Part V) — (E)
operations_table.holder: "Every conjunct is a condition on how supplied relations behave under the changes in \(C\). None inspects a label." (Part V — Account, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs. Four conjuncts run at a call on a document. The fifth reaches only as far as the document goes: HV file 54, "one of the eleven tests, *look inside*, has almost no purchase on a single document, and the skill does not say so", with the count "look inside in 3 (mode 1) and 0 (mode 2)" of sixteen. (F1) fails for want of the target's decomposition, not for want of a call. What would move it: an (F1) claim needing a change that reaches inside the target moves to "only with a record or a harness" (a rig that can intervene).

operations_table.operation: Support, critical blocks, redundant routes, interference, boundary, Pres(F) (Part VI) — (S), (B), (D)
operations_table.holder: "A block may be critical while no singleton in it is." (Part VI — Work, support, and interference, 10 and 11), with "Criticality is relative to the support \(W\) it is assessed in: a commitment critical in one successful support need not be critical in the full candidate, and the supports assessed are the ones actually written, not a support someone could write in their place." (Part VI, 11 only).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs, over the commitments its context carries. Readable in the record: pull 45 of 48 and rival 44 of 48 between markers (H64). What would move it: a partition harness, where no call sees the others' parts and a later call must assemble them, moves the row to "across calls" — that is builder B's M8b and prediction P4.3.

operations_table.operation: Representation: a faithful transport with selected or constructed provenance (Part IV) — (R)
operations_table.holder: "The carrier–content relation is thus a fidelity fact with a history." (Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance, Representation is derived, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about the agent. The fact obtains at the call if the transport's provenance obtains; nothing in the call makes it obtain and nothing in the call shows it. Establishing it needs two versions of the carrier and the reports compared, which the record has done once (file 30 against file 31: H58, H59, H62). What would move it: requiring (R) to be shown rather than to hold moves the row to "only with a record or a harness". That is the sense builder A's M4 uses, and the two senses must not be mixed (job J-C4).

operations_table.operation: Provenance of a transport: selected, constructed, declared (Part IV) — provenance
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "A transport \(t\) between organizations of a physical system has exactly one of three provenances, determined by its history in the physical module:" (Part IV — Three provenances, 10 and 11). What it needs, of the three: a history.
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about a transport. For the carriers the record holds, the record supplies the history and the theory decides: "A section of a carrier filled from another source keeps that other source's history, whatever it happens to match." (Part VIII, 11 only). For the reader's own transport the history is training, which no arrangement here supplies; builder A's M2 makes a claim about its population, not a reading of its history. What would move it: a showing that no arrangement at the grain of text can attribute a provenance to any transport the agent holds moves the row to "never".

operations_table.operation: Bearing: when an adverse signal is a criticism (K1) (Part IX) — (K1)
operations_table.holder: "An adverse signal is not a criticism until an organization represents how it bears." (Part IX — Criticism, use, and standing, Bearing, 10 and 11). In the record: HV file 52, "**Breaks.** Zero or more, each as: the quoted line of the skill, what the reader did with it, and why that is the skill's doing rather than the reader's."
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation the agent performs. The break field has (K1)'s shape — target, defect, grounds, connection — and ninety-six single-call marker agents filled it; twelve reports carried breaks the first marker had not found, "of four kinds, each quoted from the skill" (H64). What would move it: a defect whose question needs the run's history rather than the document moves the row to "only with a record or a harness".

operations_table.operation: Deployment: a representation integrated into use as a retained capability (Part X, Part XII) — Deploy
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "A capability is attributed to a system under a declared boundary (which processes and resources are the system's) and a declared continuity \(\Omega\) (what makes it the same system through change). ... Both are declared before the attribution, not chosen after it." (Part XII — System boundary and continuity, 11 only). What it needs, of the three: a declared input (the use task \(U\), the boundary, the continuity) and a history.
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about the agent, and the model attributes it to no agent (W3 section 4, last paragraph). A finite record settles it neither way: "Possibility is the absence of a law-imposed limit short of perfection on performance and retention; it is not one successful trajectory." (Part XII, 10 and 11). What would move it: it would move to "across calls" only if the use task and the boundary stopped being declared inputs, which Part XIV's declared-inputs paragraph forbids.

operations_table.operation: Building: a construction witness, bindings, "relay is not" (Part X) — Build
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "A construction witness identifies the controlled processes, the incoming carriers, the bindings constructed, and the resulting representation." (Part X — Understanding, construction, and origin, 10 and 11). What it needs, of the three: a history (an owned subhistory) and a declared boundary.
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about the agent; not attributed. The record supplies two of the witness's four for the runs a rig covers — the controlled processes (sonnet_agent_tool_audit.txt lists each agent's calls) and the incoming carriers (the prompt files sonnet_agent.py writes) — and neither the bindings constructed nor the resulting representation. What would move it: a showing that the bindings constructed cannot be identified at the grain of text at all moves the row to "never".

operations_table.operation: Newness and origin (Part X) — (N), (G)
operations_table.holder: "With \(R_{<e}(s,h)=\bigcup_{\xi\text{ before }e}R_{\beta,\ell}(s,\xi)\)," (Part X — Newness, 10 and 11), with "The repertoire \(R_{\beta,\ell}(s,\xi)\) is the set of contents deployable in some nontrivial use respect." (Part X — Deployment, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: What no arrangement at the grain of text supplies: the prior repertoire of a reader whose carrier is its weights. The union runs over every earlier \(\xi\), and the contents deployable before the arrangement began are not in the arrangement. (G) inherits this through New. A boundary declared so that \(R_{<e}\) is empty would make every content new; Part XIV forbids choosing it that way — "where the input is missing, the verdict is unsettled and the semantics says so rather than choosing the input from the verdict wanted." What would move it: a boundary declared before the attribution under which the repertoire is readable. This is not a barrier claim (Part XIII: "A finite list of failures is not a barrier proof").

operations_table.operation: Choosing histories and the index: which cases, what is held out, when to stop, what a result forces (Derivation 3, Part VIII's historical index) — \(H\), index
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "A proposition indexed to a contract remains that proposition when a later theory changes the current contract. A new index is a new claim." (Part VIII — Historical index, 10 and 11). In the record: "Before any test or research: freeze the predictions as their own numbered file first. A test plan is written before the run and not edited after." (RESEARCH-CONVENTIONS.md). What it needs, of the three: a declared input (the owner's word, the stopping rule) and the record.
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation carried by the workflow, not by the agent. The held-out set is held by a plan and by nothing in a call (W3 section 2 holds the 99 light-marked reports and the 33 sources). What would move it: a carrier handed on that held the index and the stopping rule would move it to "across calls", and that requires the owner's word to stop being a declared input.

operations_table.operation: Repair: what a change fixes and what it gives up (Part XI, (P)) — (P)
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "The obligations are declared inputs: \(O\) says what is to be repaired and \(P\) what is to be protected, each as a stated condition over stated occasions, and a protected condition is lost exactly when it fails on an occasion it covers." (Part XI — Repair, 11 only), with "\(\operatorname{ProducedBy}\) holds when an active route (Part IX) runs from \(\Delta\) to the repair". What it needs, of the three: declared inputs (\(O\), \(P\)) and a history (the active route).
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation carried by the workflow. The repository exposes losses by convention and declares no \(P\), so the exposure runs and the preservation check cannot (part C10). What would move it: the exposure alone is at one call, since a call can write what a change gives up; the check does not move, because it needs the stated occasions.

operations_table.operation: Created explanatory knowledge (Part XI) — (EK)
operations_table.holder: "(P), (EK) depend on (G), (E), Deploy." (Part XIV — Dependence order, 10 and 11), with (EK) naming \(\operatorname{Origin}(s,c,p_c,h,e_c)\) inside itself.
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about the agent; not attributed (W3 section 4, last paragraph). It inherits row 12's placement through Origin. What would move it: exactly what moves row 12, and nothing else.

operations_table.operation: Receipts and histories: leaves, derivation trees, precedence (Part IX) — receipts, \(h\)
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "A history \(h\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence \(\prec_h\) and a physical interpretation supplying process occurrences, their ports, and the connections actually instantiated." (Part IX — Histories, 10 and 11), with "An evidence leaf is a reference to an event with an interpreted claim. A receipt is a derivation tree over leaves." (Part IX — Receipts, 10 and 11). What it needs, of the three: a history.
operations_table.note: Sense: an operation carried by the workflow. The log gives the occurrences and the precedence; the rigs give the third clause for the runs they cover and the prose entries do not (part C6). The trees are built by hand — a results file cites a rig file which cites the raw returns — and no program builds one. What keeps them receipts is the convention that raw evidence is never edited, which answers "A record reconstructed from the claim it is meant to support is not a receipt for that claim." (Part IX, 11 only). What would move it to "across calls": a carrier handed on that itself supplied the precedence and the check. The Semantics two-stage packs come closest and fall short, because the hashes and the "did it do as instructed" checks are made against the repository by the orchestrator, not by the agents.

operations_table.operation: Retention and ownership: what an agent carries between calls (Part XII) — (CT1), (CT2), Can
operations_table.holder: "\(F(C)\) = states whose executions all complete and return into \(C\). \(F\) is monotone; \(C\subseteq F(C)\) is the invariant form; the union of post-fixed sets is the greatest fixed point. (CT2)" (Part XII — Retention fixed point, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: The row is mixed and is placed by its first two tags: (CT1) and (CT2) are instantiated by continuity and carry no index about the system. Can carries \(\Omega\) and \(\beta\) and so needs the declared boundary, a record item. This is the only row of the twenty-one that continuity alone places (part C12). What would move it: if the map needs Can rather than retention, the row moves to "only with a record or a harness"; and a finite record cannot establish (CT1)'s quantifier either way ("it is not one successful trajectory", Part XII). Seam: builder B's M5 says what each arm's constructor attribute is.

operations_table.operation: Scrutiny of practice: a policy becomes a target and its use changes (Part I, Part XIII) — (RC)
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "An aspect \(d\) of a system's practice is scrutinizable at \(\xi\) when there is an owned, admitted continuation in which a description of \(d\) becomes a represented target, criticism can be directed at it, and the result can affect its operative use." (Part XIII — Scrutinizability, 10 and 11), with "whether a route is active is read from the history, not from the result." (Part IX, 11 only). What it needs, of the three: a program (the read-out) and a declared boundary ("owned").
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about the agent; this is M9's row. The read-out exists only where the transport records the calls it served (run.py line 175; run_sonnet.py's tool loop). In the transport phase 4 will use, the field is the reader's own list (sonnet_agent.py: "modules_self_reported": True), and that does not move the row to "at one call", because a self-report is an emission and Derivation 9 bounds it. What would move it to "at one call": a within-call read-out the transport itself records, showing the operative use changing inside one execution.

operations_table.operation: Universality (Part XIII) — (U1)-(U3)
operations_table.holder: "Recursion does not entail universality; a historical extension does not certify it; a finite performance record does not establish it." (Part XIII — Universality, 10 and 11).
operations_table.note: What no arrangement at the grain of text supplies: \(\mathfrak E_\Theta\) and \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{adv}}_\Theta\), which (U1) and (U2) quantify over and which must be "both specified independently of the candidate". Not claimed (W3 section 6). What would move it: those two sets specified independently. A "never" here is not a barrier claim (Part XIII, Barriers).

operations_table.operation: A rule-application component: "invariant under interventions on the world and variable under edits to the rule" (Part II) — (K), rule signature
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "a **rule application** has a signature invariant under interventions on the world and variable under edits to the rule" (Part II — Kinds are edit-signatures, 10 and 11), with "Its signature under (K) is invariant under interventions on \(Z\) and variable under edits to \(C_r\)." (Part VII — Constitutive rules, 10 and 11). What it needs, of the three: a program.
operations_table.note: Sense: a predicate about a component of the arrangement. The components in this repository with that signature are programs. The record separates them from the readers: the Language checker's reports repeat identically on another machine (L69, "thirteen of its eighteen primary rig-1 ledgers run again on this machine, every report identical once timings are set aside"; L73, "all sixteen runs repeated here and identical"), while the reader's frozen question moved in two of twelve runs under identical framing (H62). What would move it to "at one call": a reader shown invariant under the changes the signature must be invariant under; the recorded drift counts against it.

operations_table.operation: The normative relation, "when a question invokes worth" (Part XIV; defined in Part XI) — \(\mathcal N\)
operations_table.column: only with a record or a harness
operations_table.holder: "The **normative relation** \(\mathcal N\), when a question invokes worth. It is taken as an input and never derived; the aesthetic relation of Part XI is one instance." (Part XIV — Primitives, 10 and 11 (reworded)), with "Where a claim invokes worth, the semantics takes a **normative relation** \(\mathcal N\) as a declared input and marks the place (Part XIV)." (Part XI — Worth, 11 only). What it needs, of the three: a declared input from outside.
operations_table.note: Sense: a primitive taken from outside, not an operation anyone performs. The input is the owner's word, kept as written in the Decisions files (part C8). What would move it: it cannot move to "at one call" — a call that derived it would refute Derivation 6 — and it would move to "never" only if no arrangement could supply the input, which the Decisions files do.

3. **Whether row 12's \"never\" would move under an honestly declared boundary.** (N) needs \\(R_{<e}\\), the union of repertoires before the episode, which no arrangement at the grain of text supplies for a reader whose carrier is its weights. A boundary declared to begin at the arrangement's first call would empty \\(R_{<e}\\) and make every content new; Part XIV forbids choosing an input from the verdict wanted, and Part XII requires the boundary to be declared before the attribution. I could not settle whether a boundary declared in advance, for reasons of its own, could honestly make the repertoire readable. The test: a declared boundary written before any attribution, with its reason, and a judge asked whether it was chosen from the verdict.

# Slice C — the practice and the map

## 1. The question, frozen

What is being explained: which of the theory's objects an agent built on a large language model instantiates at one call, which across calls, which only with a record or a harness around it, and which never — and, for this slice, where an attention policy sits (Q5), what the repository's own conventions already are in the theory's terms, and the table phase 5's skill map is drawn from (Q6). Over what range: agents of the kinds this record has run, at the declared grain of text — what is in the context, what is emitted, and what changes in the emission when the context is changed. What is asked: a *forward* question for M9 (what produces operative return), a *rule-status* question for M10 (what counts as what under the theory's definitions), and, for the table, a *blocked* question wherever a row is placed "never" (what no arrangement at this grain supplies). Not asked, and not answered: what a transformer computes at the grain of weights; whether any agent understands, is creative, or creates knowledge.

## 2. The parts and the jobs

Jobs given: Q5 and Q6, quoted from W3 section 1; Q4 is touched only at the seam with builder B. Jobs added, and named as mine: J-C1 (place every operation with a holder and say what would move it), J-C2 (the plan's job, that the repository's conventions are part of the workflow by hand), J-C3 (a read-out must be readable from the history), J-C4 (each table row must say in which sense it is placed). Three of the four are mine, so the fit between them and my parts proves little by itself, and every part that rests only on J-C2 is marked *held if*.

Parts: C1 to C5 replace M9; C6 to C10 replace M10; C11 and C12 are new and belong to the table. The sketch was not transcribed. M9 was split, because it fused a claim about the theory with a claim about an arrangement; its read-out clause was restated against the rig code; M10's history clause and its plan/assessment clause were both restated against the record and against Part 0. Each change is under "dropped" with the quotation that forced it.

## 3. Part by part

C1 *held* — the theory's list of scrutinizable aspects reaches a policy about what to read. The swap test renamed it: "an attention policy" is loose against "a method", and what is held is the list's reach. Provenance built.
C2 *held* — "represented" is (R), so text in the context is not enough. I searched file 11 for a second sense of "represent" and found none; Derivation 6 closes it. Provenance built.
C3 *held* — the reading of the router table at a call is the reader's own; the table's authorship is not. Both clauses of Part X's Ownership passage are needed and each alone gives a reading the W5 judges struck. Provenance built. No count in this programme reaches it.
C4 *held* — a trace is a read-out only where the transport records the calls it served. Held by Part IX and Part II and by the rig code: `"modules_self_reported": True` in the transport phase 4 will use. Provenance built.
C5 *held* — the recursive-class aim is the plan's declared normative input. Held by file 11's general worth paragraph, which file 10 lacked. Provenance built.
C6 to C10 *held if* — the five mappings from the repository's conventions to Parts III, VIII, IX and XI. Each carries its quoted passage; each is held *if* the plan's added job J-C2 is real, and what would settle that is P5.2. Provenance fitted throughout: they were written with the conventions in view.
C11 *held* — the table's placement rule, a construction, held between two failing swaps. Provenance built.
C12 *held if* — the table's result, that continuity alone places one operation. Held if the placements stand and by P4.1 and P4.2. Provenance built.

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Had P4.6 come out zero, the model would not have a second story ready: W3 section 8 already says the workflow's claim to the recursive class is withdrawn and M9 must say what more is needed. The model can be caught here.

**Reverse.** Poke the cause — edit the policy's words — and the trace should move; poke the effect — edit the trace after the run — and the policy does not. The sharper reverse is C4's: instruct the reader to report its modules differently and the self-reported field moves with nothing else moving, which is the signature of a measurement and not of the route.

**Hunt the answer in the starting points.** This is the strongest attack on my own table, and it is not disposed of. The column "only with a record or a harness" is defined to include "a declared input from outside", and nearly every predicate *about* the agent carries a declared index; so the conclusion "most of these operations are not at one call" could be sitting in the rule. What stops it is C11's first rider, and the rider is not free: without it every row including (E) lands in that column and the table says nothing, and with its opposite Deploy, Build, (N) and Can land at one call against Part XII's boundary sentence. The rider is drawn by the theory's words, not by the answer wanted. A judge should press here first.

**Add a job.** The rule was asked to decide a row it was not built on: the rule-application component. It places it in the record column, on the contrast between programs whose reports repeat identically (L69, L73) and a reader whose frozen question moved in two of twelve runs (H62). That job ruled out the rival "the reader is the rule component".

**Build the best rival.** The best rival to this whole slice is to place each operation by which file does the work today — W3 section 6's "Holder today" column. The two disagree on (R) and on the rule-application component, and P5.1 counts exactly that: three or fewer holder changes favours the rival, four or more favours the rule here.

**Pull.** C2 pulls against every "at one call" placement: the more is demanded of "represented", the fewer rows a call can be said to carry. The line drawn: carriage is the material being in the context, representation is the reports responding to edits of it, and the table places carriage. What would show the line in the wrong place is arm (f) — the change list withheld — moving no within-step field (P4.5): material carried and not responded to.

**Check the patches.** W5 struck M9's "outside the declared boundary" and narrowed it to "outside what the reader can make a target", recording the loss. The four restatements here are new patches and each says what it gives up. The catch-all is the record column; its gauge is that every row placed there names which of the three things it needs, and all nine do.

**Look inside.** The model says what comes out — traces, reports, marks — and not how a reader routes. Derivation 9 bounds it and no phase here reaches inside; which component of a reader decides to open a module is left unknown, with the test named as one this programme cannot run.

**What the change list leaves out.** Anything at the grain of weights; the owner's harness material, not supplied; the light-marked 99 and the 33 held-out sources, not spent.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

One: run C4's poke pair in phase 4 — delete a module file, and separately change only the reporting instruction — and take arm (r)'s trace from the transport's transcript. That single change turns P4.6 from a count on an emission into a count on a route, and it is the difference between measuring the reader's routing and measuring the reader's account of its routing.

Two: declare a protected set for one change in the repository and check that every protected condition still holds on the occasions it covers. That turns C8 and C10 from mappings into a check, and it would show whether the repository's patch rule does (P)'s work or only half of it.

## 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. The table is a reading of the theory against a record, not a result; no reader has run under it, and phase 4 is the first test. No class membership is claimed for any agent, no creativity, no knowledge, no Deploy. The three "never" placements are about what this grain supplies and are not barrier proofs — the theory says a finite list of failures is not one. The evidence cited from the record is fitting: it was read before this model was written and cannot confirm any part of it.

## 7. One next step

Before arm (r) runs, change the rig so the modules-opened field for phase 4 comes from the transport's own record of tool calls, and add the reporting-instruction box as its control. Everything M9 claims about operative return is read off that field, and as the record now keeps it, the field is the reader's report of itself.
